preview: This is the first meeting of the newly elected council, where Mayor Easton and six councillors are sworn in. Council will also name who serves as acting mayor each month, pick representatives for regional and local boards, and set the 2027 meeting schedule.

agenda_items.plain: Mayor Easton and Councillors Andersen, DesJardins, Ellis, Perreault, Prosko and Veltkamp take their oaths of office before a judge to begin their term.
agenda_items.for_you: These are the seven people who will make decisions for Squamish over the coming term.

agenda_items.plain: Council will vote on who represents Squamish on the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District Board: Mayor Easton with 5 votes, and Councillors Ellis and Andersen with 4 votes each, with Councillors Prosko, Perreault and Veltkamp as backups.
Council will vote on a rotating list of councillors who will fill in as acting mayor each month from November 2026 to December 2027.
Council will vote to appoint Councillors Andersen, Prosko and Veltkamp to the Land Back Task Force until the end of 2027.
Council will vote to appoint Councillors Ellis and Perreault to the Community Forest Board, and Councillor DesJardins to the Squamish Library Board, until the end of 2027.
Council will vote on its 2027 schedule of regular meetings, usually on the first and third Mondays of the month, with no meetings in August and one in September.
agenda_items.for_you: Regular council meetings in 2027 start at 6 p.m. at Municipal Hall, 37955 Second Avenue, with the first on January 5.

agenda_items.plain: Mayor Easton gives his opening speech for the new term, followed by remarks from each councillor.
The mayor and each councillor may invite one community member to speak to council for up to three minutes.

summary.headline: On November 3, 2026, Mayor Sean Easton and six councillors were sworn in as the new Squamish council, and council then made its first appointments to outside boards and set its 2027 meeting schedule.
key_points: A provincial court judge swore in Mayor Easton and Councillors Andersen, DesJardins, Ellis, Perreault, Prosko and Veltkamp at the Squamish Valley Golf Club.

Council named Mayor Easton, Councillor Ellis and Councillor Andersen to the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District board. Councillors Prosko, Perreault and Veltkamp are the backups. Passed with no one opposed.
Council named Councillors Andersen, Prosko and Veltkamp to the Land Back Task Force. Passed with no one opposed.
Council set a monthly rotation of acting mayors (the councillor who fills in when the mayor is away) through the end of 2027. Passed with no one opposed.
Council approved its 2027 schedule of regular meetings, usually the first and third Monday of the month, with none in August. Passed with no one opposed.
Councillor DesJardins was named to the Squamish Library Board, and Councillors Ellis and Perreault to the Community Forest Board. Both passed with no one opposed.
In his first speech, Mayor Easton said council should judge itself by results for residents, not by plans finished or effort spent.
Each council member invited one guest to speak. Topics included Brennan Park's pool and rink, support for the arts, more public consultation, and the relationship with the Squamish Nation.
explainer: This was the inaugural meeting, the first official meeting of the council elected in the fall 2026 election. It was mostly ceremony. A Squamish Nation blessing opened the evening, and a provincial court judge took each member's oath or affirmation of office.

The votes were routine start of term choices: who represents Squamish on the regional district board and other boards, who fills in as acting mayor each month, and when council will meet in 2027. Every motion passed, and the recording shows no one voting against.

Mayor Easton said he heard during the campaign that residents need housing locals can afford, more recreation, arts and cultural spaces, health and social services for all ages, and more ways to get around. He promised to involve the people affected by decisions and to be open about his work. Councillors spoke about listening, working as a team, and their relationship with the Squamish Nation. Councillor Ellis said she is leaving her job leading Housing Squamish, a non-profit housing group. Councillor Prosko named Brennan Park as one of the big decisions ahead.

The invited guests included two high school students, a former mayor, local housing leaders, a Squamish Nation hereditary chief and an elected Squamish Nation councillor. The former mayor urged council to hold public meetings before rezonings (changes to what can be built on a piece of land), survey residents before big spending, and mail out a regular newsletter. The Squamish Nation councillor welcomed the Land Back Task Force appointments. Regular council business starts at the next meetings.

decisions.title: Squamish's representatives on the regional district board
decisions.what: Squamish council voted to name Mayor Easton (holding 5 votes), Councillor Ellis (4 votes) and Councillor Andersen (4 votes) as its members on the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District board. Councillors Prosko, Perreault and Veltkamp were named as alternates (backups). The chair first forgot to read out the alternates, so council voted a second time on the full motion.
decisions.why_it_matters: These three members speak and vote for Squamish on the regional government that handles shared services across the Sea to Sky area.

decisions.title: Council members named to the Land Back Task Force
decisions.what: Squamish council voted to name Councillors Andersen, Prosko and Veltkamp to the Land Back Task Force from November 3, 2026 to December 31, 2027. The recording suggests Councillor Perreault moved it and Councillor DesJardins seconded it.
decisions.why_it_matters: The task force is part of the District's work with the Squamish Nation, and a Squamish Nation councillor welcomed it at the meeting.

decisions.title: Acting mayor rotation to the end of 2027
decisions.what: Squamish council voted to set which councillor serves as acting mayor each month from November 2026 to December 2027. Councillor Andersen takes November 2026, Councillor Ellis December 2026, and the job then rotates among all six councillors.
decisions.why_it_matters: The acting mayor fills in for the mayor when he is away.

decisions.title: 2027 council meeting schedule
decisions.what: Squamish council voted to approve its 2027 schedule of regular business meetings. They start at 6 p.m. at Municipal Hall on Second Avenue, usually twice a month, with one meeting in September and none in August.
decisions.why_it_matters: It tells residents when they can watch or attend council meetings next year.
decisions.for_you: 2027 regular meetings: January 5 and 19, February 2 and 16, March 2 and 16, April 6 and 20, May 4 and 18, June 1 and 15, July 6 and 20, September 7, October 5 and 19, November 2 and 16, December 7 and 21.

decisions.title: Council member named to the Squamish Library Board
decisions.what: Squamish council voted to name Councillor DesJardins as its member on the Squamish Library Board until December 31, 2027.

decisions.title: Council members named to the Community Forest Board
decisions.what: Squamish council voted to name Councillors Ellis and Perreault to the Community Forest Board until December 31, 2027.

decisions.title: New mayor and council sworn in
decisions.what: Squamish council's seven newly elected members took their oaths or affirmations of office before a provincial court judge. Each promised to follow conflict of interest rules, act with integrity and be accountable for their decisions.
decisions.why_it_matters: This officially starts the new council's four year term.

decisions.title: Mayor's first address and councillors' remarks
decisions.what: Squamish council heard Mayor Easton's first speech, in which he said council should be judged on whether it measurably improves residents' lives. Each councillor then spoke about what they heard during the campaign and their hopes for the term.
decisions.why_it_matters: The speeches give a first sense of the priorities the new council members say they will bring.

decisions.title: Guests invited by the mayor and council
decisions.what: Squamish council heard from one guest invited by each member. A student asked for more support for the arts and repairs to the local theatre. Another student asked council to make Brennan Park's pool and rink a priority. A former mayor urged public meetings before rezonings, surveys before big spending, and a mailed newsletter. Squamish Nation leaders spoke about building the relationship between the two governments.
decisions.why_it_matters: These guests named some of the issues residents may see come to council this term.
